riskReasons: Pro forma is built on only 2 franchised locations — a very thin sample; treat the modeled franchisee economics as low-confidence.
Capital gap of $3,059,250 is ~12x your liquid — extreme leverage; the deal rests almost entirely on outside capital.
2 high-severity operational tripwires disclosed — see the tripwires section.
Franchisor financial distress disclosed (going-concern doubt) — confirm its ability to support the system against the audited statements.
notes: Item 19 in this filing also publishes 2 tables that are not gross sales — patient or visit counts, a profit-and-loss table, or pre-sale figures. They are excluded from the top line, which is built only on disclosed gross revenue.

underwriting.assessment: With $250,000 liquid against a $3,309,250 mid-point build-out, there is a $3,059,250 capital gap. An SBA loan or an equity partner is required to do this deal. At mid-cohort revenue, about $44,722/mo is left after fees, rent and debt service — cost of goods and labor still come out of that, and the cash ladder below subtracts them.

benchmark.rampNote: 6–18 months to a mature membership/booking base; the Item 19 average is NOT a year-one number.
considerations: Budget blended COGS ~15–28% (sim time and memberships carry little; the bar and kitchen drive it) and labor ~22–30%.
Decide owner-operator vs. absentee before modeling — absentee adds a GM salary (~$60–90K/yr) the pro forma omits.
Confirm the F&B attach rate and per-bay equipment costs (e.g. simulator licenses, R&M) at mature franchised units via Item 20.
Assume a 6–18 month ramp; discount the Item 19 mature average for year one.

financialCondition.headline: The franchisor's own auditor has raised substantial doubt about whether it can stay in business — a serious signal for a company you'd depend on for years of support.
body: What we found (2025, audited by Armanino LLP): Net loss of $1.64M on $718K of revenue — roughly 3.3x spent per $1 earned. Losses are widening, not shrinking. Negative net worth (a members'/stockholders' deficit) of $3.14M, and deepening year over year. Total liabilities are about 7.4x total assets. About 70% of liabilities is money owed to related parties — the entity is kept alive largely by insider loans, not profit. Cash of $257K against $1.11M of obligations due within a year (a current ratio of 0.32). Note: about 30% of those liabilities is deferred revenue — prepaid franchise fees the company owes as future services, not borrowed money. Netting it out, liabilities are still about 5.1x assets.

Why it matters to you: field support, training, technology, and marketing come out of the franchisor's budget. If outside funding slows, those are the first things to get cut. There is no parent guarantee of performance in this FDD, so The Range NYC LLC is not contractually obligated to keep funding the franchisor or backing its commitments to you.

Verify before you commit: ask for the most recent interim (unaudited) financials and the current-year funding plan; ask whether the parent will sign a guarantee of performance; and cross-check Item 20 — unit closures, transfers, and terminations are the operational tell that corroborates financial stress.
aggravators: the auditor raised substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern
negative net worth that is deepening year over year
more due within a year than current assets to cover it
heavy dependence on related-party loans to stay funded
no parent guarantee backing the franchisor's obligations to you
financialCondition.evidenceNote: Flagged on the FDD's "Special Risks" page and grounded in the Item 21 / Exhibit F audited financials. Figures are extracted; all ratios and grading are computed. Confirm against the source statements and a CPA before relying on them.
